No specialized discussions of this poem appear in the provided secondary literature dossier. However, computational analysis conducted by DharmaNexus reveals substantial Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 410 matching segments across 58 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most significant textual parallel is preserved in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which incorporates the narrative almost entirely, matching segments §0.3–32.4 with high textual similarity [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares standard stock formulas and verses with multiple companion apadānas within the Therīapadāna—including those of Paṭācārā (Thi-Ap 20), Kuṇḍalakesā (Thi-Ap 21), Kisāgotamī (Thi-Ap 22), Dhammadinnā (Thi-Ap 23), and Nandā (Thi-Ap 25)—as well as several Thera-apadāna discourses and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language automated alignment also detects minor shared stock passages in Chinese (T 63), Sanskrit (*Kaṭhināvadāna*), and Tibetan translations (such as the *Śrāvakabhūmi*, D 4036), though these constitute generic text-reuse matches rather than direct doctrinal parallels [DharmaNexus].
